title: The Pulse, Wednesday 10 September 2026
tldr: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra with looped transformers, computer use, and reasoning effort controls—it's their new flagship for work and a direct shot at Claude's agent niche. Shopify acquired Tailwind CSS. OpenRouter launched US in-region routing alongside their existing EU option, keeping inference inside national borders.

research.title: An Experimental Evaluation of Multimodal Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic AI Frameworks
research.summary: MMPIBench evaluates image-based prompt injection on multi-modal agents that can call tools and access files; agents frequently obey instructions hidden in images.
research.why: Multi-modal agents are a next step for voice workflows; knowing the image-injection surface matters before we put images into agent context.

research.title: AgentAudit: An Open, Extensible Framework for Full-Lifecycle Trust Evaluation of AI Agents
research.summary: Evaluation framework covering the complete agent pipeline—planning, tool selection, execution, memory, reasoning—instead of just task completion.
research.why: Our agent QA needs to pinpoint where failures happen; this offers a structured way to test each stage separately.

research.title: KVShareArena: KV-Cache Reuse Across Contexts and Model Checkpoints
research.summary: Reuses KV caches when retrieved chunks appear mid-prompt instead of only at the start, targeting RAG and multi-agent report reading.
research.why: RAG with dynamic chunk order is our Pipeline retrieval pattern; cache reuse here would cut prefill costs noticeably.

research.title: Subagents vs Agent Skills: Executing Reusable Knowledge for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
research.summary: Compares multi-file skill packages with spawning subagents for reusable capabilities; finds skills more reliable for deterministic subtasks.
research.why: Hermes uses skill packages heavily; this validates the approach and tells us when to prefer skills over delegation.

research.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
research.summary: Parallel memory updates instead of sequential segment reading to handle extremely long contexts more efficiently.
research.why: Long context appears in our legislative research and call transcripts; faster memory updates would help agents stay under latency budgets.

releases.title: Node.js v26.8.2 (Current)
releases.summary: Current release with OpenSSL 3.5.8, Undici 8.10.2, and riscv64 build improvements.
releases.why: We track Current for upcoming LTS features; this brings security updates we'll inherit when 26 becomes LTS.

releases.title: langchain-openai 1.6.2
releases.summary: Adds GPT-6 Astra reasoning effort support and bumps httpx2 to 2.12.0.
releases.why: LangChain catching up to GPT-6 Astra's new API means we can test reasoning effort in our SalesKick flows today.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.33.0
releases.summary: Optional startTime on observation GET, has/-has: filter hints, prompt name in playground, and performance improvements.
releases.why: Langfuse observability covers our agent calls; the playground prompt-name feature helps debug chains faster.

hackernews.title: GPT-6 Astra, looped transformers, and hidden reasoning
hackernews.summary: Sebastian Raschka's deep dive on GPT-6 Astra's looped transformer architecture, cost tradeoffs, and whether reasoning traces remain visible.
hackernews.why: GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's new flagship; understanding the architecture matters when we evaluate it against Claude for agent work.

hackernews.title: Shopify acquires Tailwind
hackernews.summary: Adam Wathan and the Tailwind team join Shopify; Tailwind CSS remains MIT-licensed and development continues.
hackernews.why: We use Tailwind across Pipeline, SalesKick, and our internal tools; this keeps it resourced but shifts governance to Shopify.

hackernews.title: DeepSeek launching v4.1 flash cheaper and more capable than v4 pro
hackernews.summary: DeepSeek v4.1 flash beats v4 pro on benchmarks at lower cost; discussion on whether the pro tier still makes sense.
hackernews.why: We evaluate DeepSeek for cost-sensitive production workloads; a cheaper model that beats the expensive one shifts our testing priorities.

hackernews.title: Claude, change the "Add to Cart" button to blue
hackernews.summary: Live demo of Claude editing a running e-commerce site via natural language commands; 1065 points, strong execution discussion.
hackernews.why: Direct UI manipulation with NL commands is a pattern we're exploring for campaign editing; this shows a polished version of that interaction.

hackernews.title: Qwen 3.8 follows GPT-5.5 Pro reasoning prefills
hackernews.summary: Qwen 3.8 appears to use a reasoning prefill structure similar to GPT-5.5 Pro; gist analyzes the prompt format.
hackernews.why: Reasoning prefills shape how we structure agent prompts; knowing Qwen adopted this pattern helps us write portable prompts.

x_posts.title: François Chollet: ZeroModels
x_posts.summary: François Chollet announced ZeroModels—100+ model families with pretrained weights in Keras 3, backend-agnostic.
x_posts.why: ZeroModels plus KerasHub gives us a unified interface to run foundation models across backends; simplifies model eval and switching.

x_posts.title: Coding agent setup with shared brain
x_posts.summary: Thread on setting up Agentic Stack as a local shared knowledge layer across multiple coding agents to avoid re-explaining the project.
x_posts.why: Our agents (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes) all re-learn the same project context; a shared brain pattern would cut onboarding token costs.

x_posts.title: OpenAI DevDay Exchange events
x_posts.summary: OpenAI announced DevDay Exchange—local builder meetups with OpenAI team participation in multiple cities.
x_posts.why: Worth tracking for learning about GPT-6 Astra usage patterns from early adopters and OpenAI's developer strategy.

closing: Models: no new releases on OpenRouter or Hugging Face in the window.
